dct_description_sm: The purpose of this project was to collect, analyze and disseminate information regarding the state and health of the sea ice ecosystems in Hudson Bay and its relationship to the socio-economic environment in the Inuit communities that rely on these habitats. The short-term objectives were to: 1) Develop and implement Community Based Research and Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit (IQ) Monitoring that address cumulative impacts of environmental change (climate and cumulative impacts of hydroelectric mega-projects) on sea ice ecosystems in southeast Hudson Bay, 2) Implement Community Monitoring Data Portal to improve data management techniques and making information accessible to Nunavummiut and decision makers, as well as providing a forum for sharing knowledge between IQ holders and scientists, and 3) Analysis of data for evaluating environmental trends and cumulative impacts, and dissemination of results. The long-term objectives were to: 1) Develop a multi-community based monitoring network tracking sea ice, oceanography and wildlife across regions of Hudson Bay, and 2) To provide information on the cumulative impacts of environmental change needed for use in decision-making, results-based wildlife and ecosystems management, economic development and in establishing national and international policies and thresholds for hydroelectric energy storage and distribution that work with the seasons of the hydrological cycle, reducing their impacts on sea ice ecosystems.
